proposals.title: Re-attempt monorepo bootstrap using npm workspaces, eliminating pnpm entirely
proposals.why_now: TASK-0001 has been rejected 3 consecutive times. Every rejection traces to pnpm binary resolution in the authoritative validation environment. Attempt-3 introduced a pnpm shim that was explicitly rejected (REVIEW-002) for falsely reporting installation success. Switching to npm workspaces with npm ci as the installation command removes the root cause without any shim. All subsequent FASE-1 work — ADRs, packages/core, world, domain, Electron, installers — is blocked until this foundation is accepted.

proposals.title: Write ADR-002 (hash function), ADR-004 (rounding enforcement), and ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder) before packages/core
proposals.why_now: §15 FASE-1 acceptance states ADR-009 must be written and the CanonicalEncoder implemented before any state hash exists. ADR-002 requires the hash function specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before any rand() implementation. ADR-004's DEFINIR on rounding-mode enforcement must be resolved before the division helper can be correctly typed. Implementing packages/core without these ADRs embeds unrecorded decisions that cannot be reversed without an encodingVersion bump invalidating all frozen reference StateHashes. These docs can be written in parallel with IDEA-001 and unblock IDEA-003.

proposals.title: packages/core — branded numeric types, positional RNG, division helpers, and CanonicalEncoder
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the dependency of every other pure package. Without branded types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate as bigint; Tick and noise indices as safe-integer number), ADR-003 and ADR-004 have no enforcement mechanism and violations accumulate from the first file of any dependent package. Without rand() implementing ADR-002 bit-exactly, packages/world cannot be written. Without CanonicalEncoder implementing ADR-009, no StateHash can be computed and INV-01, INV-17, INV-22 have no foundation. This is the second foundational implementation step after the monorepo and required ADRs are accepted.

proposals.title: packages/world (2-octave price generator), packages/domain (ledger + market orders), packages/application (canonical tick loop and save)
proposals.why_now: These three packages compose the functional core required for FASE-1 acceptance. The price generator delivers INV-02 (described by the spec as the most important test in the project). The double-entry multi-commodity ledger delivers INV-04 through INV-07. The canonical ten-step tick loop from §7 is explicitly listed in FASE-1 acceptance criteria. The save structure per ADR-006 enables the CLI replay tool. None of these invariants can be verified in isolation — they become testable only when composed through application, which is the layer that legally couples world and domain without creating a package-level import between them.

proposals.title: tools/replay, tools/bench, minimum Electron UI, CI matrix, and installers to complete FASE-1
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires: tools/replay reporting the first divergent tick; tools/bench with calibration micro-benchmark and frozen ratio baseline in a versioned file; minimum UI (lightweight-charts price chart, BRL balance, buy/sell market order buttons, pause and 1x controls, permanent non-dismissable disclaimer in Portuguese per §20); simulation running in the dedicated worker not the renderer thread; Windows and Linux installers produced by CI. The performance baseline must be frozen in FASE-1 — deferring tools/bench means there is no reference for regressions in all subsequent phases. §14.6 explicitly identifies deferred packaging as the most likely cause of ABI and module-native failures discovered too late to fix.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — transcendental functions for price generation: §5.1 constructs prices in log-space requiring operations such as Math.log and Math.exp. §13 prohibits both in pure packages (packages/world is pure). An ADR specifying a fixed-point or lookup-table implementation producing bit-identical cross-platform results must be written and accepted before packages/world can implement the price generator. This ADR is a prerequisite for IDEA-004 and is distinct from ADR-002, ADR-004, and ADR-009.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — octave parameters: the number of octaves, periods, and amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are explicitly DEFINIR per §5.1 and must be fixed in a versioned configuration file with an ADR before the price generator is implemented, because any post-implementation change requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes frozen in tools/bench.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — tools/* dependency edges: §14.5 defines directed edges for packages/ and apps/ but not for tools/*. tools/replay and tools/bench must import from packages to fulfill FASE-1 acceptance. The allowed import edges for tools/ must be resolved in a SPEC_BLOCKERS.md entry or ADR before those tools acquire cross-workspace imports.
